pages.title: Control Plane (Cloudflare Workers)
pages.purpose: Covers the Worker entrypoint (fetch, scheduled crons, queue consumers), the API router with per-route authentication policies, D1-backed stores, and the platform bindings (DO, KV, R2, queues, service auth) that compose the control plane.
instructions: Durations in milliseconds with _MS suffix.
GitHub App private keys must be PKCS#8 format for Cloudflare Workers.
No checked-in wrangler.toml: control-plane config is generated by Terraform; DO bindings need a two-phase Terraform deploy (bindings disabled, then enabled).
Route handlers must use ctx.db (instrumented D1) instead of raw env.DB — an ESLint rule forbids .DB access under src/routes and src/webhooks.

pages.title: System Architecture Overview
pages.purpose: Describes the three-tier topology (web client → Cloudflare control plane → sandbox data plane), the bot workers, the package dependency graph, and the canonical prompt/data flow so changes can be traced across service boundaries.
instructions: Build @open-inspect/shared first whenever shared types change; other packages import from it at build time.
Data flow: user prompt → web client → control plane session DO (WebSocket) → sandbox → streaming events back through the same WebSocket chain; document this canonical path when assessing any change.

pages.title: Persistence: D1, DO SQLite, R2, KV
pages.purpose: Maps where state lives: per-session SQLite in the DO vs. D1 global stores (session index, automations, secrets, environments, image builds, skills, users, integration settings, pull-request records), encrypted columns, R2 media, KV caches, and D1 migrations.
instructions: Integration tests share one D1 instance — use cleanD1Tables() or equivalent cleanup in beforeEach/afterEach to avoid cross-test pollution.
Migrations live in terraform/d1/migrations and are applied via scripts/d1-migrate.sh and by test/integration/apply-migrations.ts.
Secrets are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM; token encryption keys are env validation gates (see src/env-validation.ts).

pages.title: Sandbox Provider Abstraction and Infra Packages
pages.purpose: Documents the pluggable SandboxProvider interface (Modal, Daytona, E2B, OpenComputer, Vercel Sandboxes), provider REST clients, the SandboxLifecycleManager decision engine (spawn/snapshot/restore/circuit-breaker/warm), and the infra packages that build provider templates/images.
instructions: Create-bind-launch contract for image builds: create build sandbox, bind provider session id via onProviderSessionCreated, then launch.

Modal deployments: never deploy src/app.py directly; run uv run python deploy.py --build-sandbox-image before uv run modal deploy deploy.py (or deploy -m src). Update CACHE_BUSTER in packages/modal-infra/src/images/base.py to force an image rebuild.
Modal timeouts are in seconds; control plane passes providerSessionTimeoutSeconds verbatim — adapters resolve it, providers apply it.
Providers declare capabilities (timeout, snapshots, restore, persistent resume, explicit stop); lifecycle decisions must respect them.

pages.title: Sandbox Runtime (in-sandbox Python agent)
pages.purpose: Covers the Python runtime that boots inside every sandbox: supervisor lifecycle, the bridge WebSocket to the control plane, OpenCode server management, repository sync, git signing and the git credential helper, diff capture, managed-skills materialization, agent tools, and provider auth plugins.
instructions: BootMode (fresh / snapshot_restore / repo_image / build) is derived from process env in runtime_config.py and drives repository boot behavior.
Durations in seconds with _seconds suffix in Python.

Git credential helper: a successful response is cached to /run/oi/scm-creds.json (mode 0600); the cache is never a fallback for a failed refresh — stale tokens silently authenticating are worse than visible failures.
Git is always invoked with argument arrays — repository paths and filenames are never interpolated into a shell command.

pages.title: Session Durable Object Runtime
pages.purpose: Explains the per-session DO: composition root (components.ts builds the whole collaborator graph), SQLite schema, internal HTTP dispatcher/handlers, WebSocket hub with hibernation, message queue, event stream, and DO alarm scheduling.
instructions: Schema is shared between SCHEMA_SQL (fresh DOs) and migration 31 (existing DOs) so the paths cannot diverge.
SessionDO.ensureInitialized() applies the schema then eagerly builds the runtime; a throw leaves the activation uninitialized so the next event retries — preserve this retry behavior.
SessionInternalPaths constants in session/contracts.ts are shared between router and DO — never hardcode internal paths; both sides must import them to prevent drift.

pages.title: Web Client (Next.js)
pages.purpose: Covers the Next.js app: session dashboard and session view, settings surfaces, API proxy routes that forward to the control plane, session socket hook/transport, browser auth proxies, and middleware correlation headers.
instructions: Browser auth is origin-bound: a production control plane cannot authenticate a localhost web process (WEB_APP_URL must match).
NEXT_PUBLIC_WS_URL must be available at build time (Next.js inlines NEXT_PUBLIC_* into the client bundle).
The web app proxies most API calls to the control plane signed with sig1 service auth; the control plane is the sole sign-in-provider authority and holds repository credentials.

pages.title: Automations: Triggers, Conditions, and Runs
pages.purpose: Documents the automation model (schedule/webhook/Sentry/GitHub/Slack triggers, condition registry, invocation/run fan-out per repository or environment, provider-auth pinning), the D1-backed scheduler, callback delivery, and webhook auth.
instructions: Every firing records one automation_invocations row plus one automation_runs child per repository/environment target — there is no separate single-repo pipeline.
Scheduler caps: MAX_PER_TICK=25 automations, TICK_CHILD_LAUNCH_BUDGET=50 child launches, AUTOMATION_LAUNCH_CONCURRENCY=4; leftover overdue work is picked up next tick.
Triggered sessions are sessions: they go through initializeSession and the DO init path.
Webhook API keys and Sentry client secrets are encrypted and HMAC-verified per automation.

pages.title: Environments and Repository Metadata
pages.purpose: Documents environments (named ordered repository sets with environment secrets and optional prebuilt images), repository metadata (defaultEnvironmentId routing), channel/team associations, and how each launch surface resolves a session target to an environment.
instructions: Environment sessions receive global + environment secrets only; repository secrets never flow into environment launches (an environment is curated).
GitHub-bot fallback: if repository metadata's defaultEnvironmentId lookup fails or the environment no longer contains the trigger repo, resolution fails open to a repo-bound session.
resolveEnvironmentTarget snapshots the environment's members at create time; environment_id records provenance on the session.

pages.title: Managed Skills
pages.purpose: Covers the managed-skills subsystem: shared skills, assignments, personal profiles, content-addressed revisions, git import/reimport, immutable session resolution manifests, and sandbox-side materialization into the OpenCode global config.
instructions: Managed skills are trusted content, not a permission boundary — call that out whenever evaluating skill-installed tooling.

Sandbox-side limits: MAX_SKILL_FILES=100, MAX_SKILL_FILE_BYTES=256KiB, MAX_SKILL_REVISION_BYTES=1MiB; revisions are fetched in windows of 50 because per-file JSON framing does not count against the manifest ceiling.
resolveManagedSkills retries catalog generation checks so the returned digest never mixes rows from different catalog states.

pages.title: Models and Provider Accounts
pages.purpose: Documents the shared model catalog (Anthropic/OpenAI/xAI/OpenCode Zen/Z.AI/DeepSeek), reasoning efforts, subscription-backed provider accounts (ChatGPT, SuperGrok) with device authorization, credential adapters, session provider-auth snapshots, and unattended-mode selection policy.
instructions: Never fail over implicitly to another paid account — failure policy keeps explicit selection stable.
Provider accounts are installation-wide (single tenant); OpenAI/xAI device auth returns refresh tokens to the control plane only — they are never shown in the browser or copied through the sandbox.
Sessions pin provider-auth rows at creation and never consult moving defaults during token refresh; children inherit parent auth rows and cannot override them.

pages.title: Pre-Built Images (Image Build Subsystem)
pages.purpose: Explains the image-build lifecycle: repo vs environment scopes, fingerprinting, planning, provider adapters, callback auth, the finalization queue, maintenance/reaper, rebuild policy, and how sandbox boot modes consume built images.
instructions: Callbacks are authorized with hashed callback tokens and a pepper (IMAGE_CALLBACK_TOKEN_PEPPER) via callback-auth.ts.
Configured provider always travels with its planner (ImageBuildProviderDeps); the invalid provider-without-planner state is unconstructible.

Part of the deployment selects which providers support images: modal, vercel, opencomputer build artifacts; daytona uses persistent sandboxes and e2b uses pause/resume — image settings are disabled for those backends.

pages.title: Secrets: Scopes, Encryption, and Injection
pages.purpose: Covers global/repo/environment secret scopes, precedence rules, encrypted storage, validation, and how a session's final environment-var set is resolved for sandbox injection.
instructions: Managed OAuth refresh tokens are never injected into sandboxes; only short-lived material is brokered.
Precedence: repo/environment secrets override global keys with the same name; on ad-hoc multi-repo collision the primary repository wins.
REPO_SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY and TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY are required gates — misconfigured deployments fail at session init, not at first spawn.

pages.title: Sessions: Targets, State, and Lifecycle Model
pages.purpose: Defines the session data model: session targets (single repo, multi-repo up to 10, environment, or none), participants, messages/events/artifacts, sandbox state references, session index/inbox records, statuses, and parent/child lineage.
instructions: A repo_owner may contain / (GitLab subgroups); only repo_name is a single path segment — use shared repository identity helpers, never split owners on first /.
Multi-repo sessions: first repository is primary and drives defaults; pushes/PRs are per-repository.
Repository context must include repoOwner, repoName, and repoId together; no-repo sessions must not include branch context.
initializeSession writes D1 index first, then initializes the DO — this ordering is an invariant: failures must be caught before any sandbox spawn.

pages.title: GitHub Integration (github-bot + webhooks)
pages.purpose: Covers the GitHub bot worker (webhook signature, delivery dedupe, auto-review of new PRs, @mention/review-thread triggers, autofix ingress) plus control-plane internal webhooks: normalized github event routing, automation matching, and PR lifecycle tracking.
instructions: Auto-review skips draft PRs, self-origin PRs (GitHub App bot), out-of-scope repos, and disallowed trigger senders.

The control-plane /internal/github-event route forwards normalized events to the scheduler and piggybacks PR lifecycle tracking in the background — lifecycle failures never affect automation matching.
Webhook deliveries are deduped via KV (7-day TTL) and signature-verified with X-Hub-Signature-256.

pages.title: Linear Integration (linear-bot)
pages.purpose: Covers the Linear agent worker: AgentSessionEvent webhooks, issue → session creation, follow-up prompts to the same session, stop/cancel handling, repo/environment target resolution, model resolution, and the opt-in issue state transition.
instructions: Follow-up comments on an issue with an active session are sent as additional prompts to the existing session, never new sessions.
Issue state transition is opt-in and best-effort — a skipped, rejected, or failed transition never blocks agent execution.
The bot uses client-credentials app-actor tokens (30-day) for runtime API calls and HMAC-signed callbacks to control plane.

pages.title: Slack Integration (slack-bot)
pages.purpose: Covers the Slack bot worker: event handling and signature verification, LLM classifier for target resolution, target clarification pickers, thread-session continuity, App Home preferences, channel triggers, completion delivery via Cloudflare Queue, and agent-initiated Slack notifications.
instructions: Completion replies are delivered asynchronously through a Cloudflare Queue; media delivery is bounded (5 files, 10MiB each, 25MiB total per completion).
Inbound images use files:read; generated media posted back requires files:write — adding scopes requires reinstalling the app per workspace.
The bot signs control-plane calls with sig1 service auth and its own secret; SLACK_BOT_TOKEN enables agent-initiated chat.postMessage only when AGENT_SLACK_NOTIFY_ENABLED is set in the sandbox.

pages.title: Trigger System and Inbound Webhooks
pages.purpose: Documents the shared trigger framework (schedule, github_event, linear_event, sentry, webhook, slack_event), condition registry, normalized event envelopes, control-plane webhook routes (sentry/automation/github/slack), and sig1 service-to-service auth.
instructions: New trigger types must be added to automationTriggerTypeSchema, the registry, and the condition catalog together; shared schemas are the boundary contract for the bots.
Sentry webhook verifies HMAC with the automation's stored encrypted client secret; verify signature before any expensive work.
sig1 canonical request layout is pinned by immutable golden vectors in test-fixtures/service-auth-vectors.json — any layout change requires a new format tag (sig2), never an edit in place.

pages.title: Deployment, Terraform, and CI/CD
pages.purpose: Documents full-stack deployment via Terraform (Cloudflare, Vercel/OpenNext, Modal/Daytona/E2B/OpenComputer/Vercel Sandboxes), D1 migrations, environment variables, GitHub Actions auto-deploy, and operational scripts.
instructions: CI pushes to main auto-deploy: terraform triggers control plane + D1 migrations + (cloudflare) web; vercel triggers web; modal triggers data plane.
Durable Object binding changes require two-phase Terraform (enable_durable_object_bindings=false → true).
Single-tenant only: deploy behind org SSO/VPN, install the GitHub App only on intended repos, restrict sign-in (ALLOWED_USERS / ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS / ALLOWED_GITHUB_ORGS).
Terraform needs Cloudflare token with Workers, KV, R2, D1, Queues Edit; Queues:Edit is required for image-build finalization.
web_platform chooses vercel (default) or cloudflare (OpenNext) — with cloudflare, Vercel credentials are dummy defaults.

pages.title: Logging, Correlation, and Debugging
pages.purpose: Covers the common structured-log envelope, canonical correlation IDs (trace_id, request_id, session_id, sandbox_id), HTTP header propagation, cross-service joining, and the cf-logs tooling for querying worker logs.
instructions: A prompt run crosses slack-bot → control-plane → modal-infra → sandbox; join on trace_id from the entry edge.
Canonical correlation keys are snake_case outside local in-memory variables; HTTP headers use x-trace-id, x-request-id, x-session-id, x-sandbox-id — convert once at boundaries, never mix casings.
msg field is a stable event identifier; use it for querying, not free-form text.

pages.title: Testing Conventions
pages.purpose: Documents test layout and harnesses across packages: co-located Vitest unit tests, control-plane workerd integration pool (Miniflare + real D1), Python pytest for modal-infra/sandbox-runtime, module-boundary and lint-complexity checks, and key test helpers.
instructions: Integration tests share one D1 instance — clean D1 tables in beforeEach/afterEach; migrations applied via test/integration/apply-migrations.ts; helpers: initSession(), queryDO(), seedEvents().
Python uses pytest + pytest-asyncio; ruff check --fix && ruff format for Python linting.
Run npm run typecheck and lint:complexity before considering a change complete; build @open-inspect/shared first for typecheck to succeed.
TypeScript uses Vitest: unit tests co-located as src/**/*.test.ts; control-plane integration tests use cloudflareTest() in workerd with real D1 bindings.

pages.title: Child Sessions (Parallel Sub-Tasks)
pages.purpose: Documents agent-spawned child sessions: spawn API, depth caps, concurrency/total limits, admission leases, child summary/update contracts, and the sandbox-side spawn-child tool.
instructions: Child admission uses lease tokens (CHILD_ADMISSION_LEASE_TTL_MS=5min) and the recursive descendant CTE is capped (MAX_DESCENDANT_DEPTH=10) to guard against parent_session_id cycles.
MAX_SPAWN_DEPTH=2; children inherit parent provider-auth rows and sandbox settings; agent child-spawn requests cannot override auth.
Sandbox-side tools spawn-child / send-child-prompt / get-child-status / cancel-child form the agent-facing contract; keep tool wire formats in sync with control-plane spawn contracts.

pages.title: Pull Requests, SCM Credentials, and Autofix
pages.purpose: Covers branch naming/resolution, PR creation with user-vs-bot attribution, head-branch reuse (force-push vs new PR), PR snapshot syncing to session artifacts, webhook-driven PR lifecycle tracking, and the GitHub autofix review-feedback pipeline.
instructions: One open PR per head branch: creating again force-pushes and reuses the PR (response marks updated:true); merged/closed PRs release the head branch.
PR creation uses the prompting user's OAuth token when available (proper attribution); users without SCM tokens fall back to the shared GitHub App bot.
PR lifecycle tracking is additive and best-effort: a failure never affects automation matching; identity is (repository_external_id, pr_number) first, branch-name derivation is a guarded fallback.
The in-sandbox git credential helper calls POST /sessions/:id/scm-credentials (sandbox-authenticated) and caches until near expiry; stale credentials must never authenticate.

pages.title: Session Diffs (Changes Capture)
pages.purpose: Explains the git-backed diff capture protocol between sandbox runtime and control plane: immutable base commit comparison, bounded patch bundles with versioned schema, the session-diff store/retry/failure protocol, and UI consumption.
instructions: Capture limits are bounded (max files 1000, patch 512KiB, bundle 1.5MiB) and files are classified renderable/metadata_only/too_large/binary.
Git is always invoked with argument arrays; repository paths and filenames are never interpolated into a shell command.
SESSION_DIFF_VERSION is mirrored between Python and shared TS — keep both in sync on any schema change.

pages.title: Session Lifecycle: Create, Spawn, Prompt, Stream, Stop
pages.purpose: Traces the end-to-end runtime flow: session creation and DO init, sandbox spawn/restore decisions (with circuit breaker, inactivity, heartbeat, warm decisions), prompt enqueue and message queue processing, streaming events, alarms/timeouts, and archive/draft sweep.
instructions: Alarm handler checks stuck processing messages (execution timeout) before delegating to lifecycle alarms; processing is idempotent.
D1 is written before the DO is initialized; failures must be caught before any sandbox spawn (invariant).
Provider and SCM factory construction is eager and throws on misconfigured deployments — fail at session init, never run degraded.
SandboxLifecycleManager uses pure decision functions (decisions.ts) for policy and injected dependencies for side effects; it owns the isSpawningSandbox flag to prevent concurrent spawns.

pages.title: Open-Inspect Repository Wiki — Quickstart
pages.purpose: Entry point that maps every task a coding agent might have (where a subsystem lives, which flow a change touches, where invariants live) to the wiki's folder hierarchy: architecture, concepts, workflows, integrations, operations, testing.
instructions: Always build @open-inspect/shared before any package that imports it (control-plane, web, slack-bot, github-bot, linear-bot).
Durations: milliseconds in TypeScript (suffix _MS), seconds in Python (suffix _seconds); never use a bare timeout.

Route readers to the folder hierarchy per task: architecture for how the system is composed, concepts for data model and configuration, workflows for end-to-end flows, integrations for the bots/triggers, operations for deploy/debug, testing for test conventions.

This repo is a single-tenant background coding agent system; all users share the same GitHub App installation scope and can access any repository the App can reach — never assume per-user repo access validation.
